stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist learns informally that her supervising physician surrendered his federal controlled substances registration last month. His medical licence is unrestricted and she has received no notice from any board. May she continue co-managing patients this afternoon?

choices.text: No, because the physician is deemed ineligible on that surrender alone.
Yes, because his medical licence remains unrestricted.
Yes, because no board has notified her that anything has changed.
Yes, because only a state registration event affects the collaboration.
Yes, provided she confines herself to non-controlled therapies today.

explanation.core_reasoning: 243 CMR 2.12(3)(d) deems a physician ineligible to participate in collaborative drug therapy management where he has voluntarily surrendered, or has had suspended, revoked or restricted, a controlled substances licence, permit or registration, EITHER STATE OR FEDERAL. The medical licence being intact does not save it, and notification to the pharmacist is discretionary for the Board, so the absence of notice proves nothing.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the surrender alone renders him ineligible.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation makes the registration event sufficient on its own.
choice_analysis.C: Notification is discretionary, so silence is not reassurance.
choice_analysis.D: The regulation names state or federal events alike.
choice_analysis.E: The ineligibility goes to the collaboration itself, not to the drugs involved.

related_facts: Board notification to the pharmacist is permitted rather than required
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates wait for formal notice, which the regulation does not guarantee will ever come.

reasoning_steps: Identify the event as a controlled substances registration surrender
Note that state and federal events count equally
Note that notice to the pharmacist is discretionary
